about: Reference list /gramatica/lista-de-verbos-reflexivos (Portuguese: reflexive and pronominal verbs). items: [verb, forms (eu presente · ele/ela perfeito simples · particípio), example, level]; a string starting with '# ' is a sub-heading. Section ids are kept from the German list: trennbar = daily routine and the body, untrennbar = with a fixed preposition, beides = the pronoun changes the meaning, three-part = feelings and change. The worksheet builds sentences from the trennbar examples and the live quiz asks for the eu form with its pronoun, so every eu form ends in the enclitic `-me` (European enclisis: levanto-me). *…* in regel becomes bold. Brazil puts the pronoun before the verb in speech (me levanto); see ptBR.

ptBR.note: In Brazil the pronoun usually comes first in speech and writing: Eu me levanto. Portugal: Levanto-me (enclisis); proclisis only after não, que, já, etc.

title: Reflexive and pronominal verbs
metaTitle: Portuguese reflexive and pronominal verbs: list with examples – Reference – icanspeak Portuguese
description: Common European Portuguese reflexive and pronominal verbs with their forms and an example: daily routine, verbs with a fixed preposition, and verbs where the pronoun changes the meaning.
lead: Verbs that come with a pronoun: me, te, se, nos, se. Each one has its forms and an example. The rule is above each list.
practice: Pronouns after the verb: vejo-o, dá-me
Verbs of change: ficar, tornar-se, passar a

sections.name: Daily routine and the body
sections.what: You do the action to yourself. The pronoun changes with the person: levanto-me, levantas-te, levanta-se.
regel: The pronoun goes with the person: *levanto-me, levantas-te, levanta-se, levantamo-nos, levantam-se.* (With *nós* the -s of the verb drops: *levantamo-nos.*)

In a plain statement the pronoun comes after the verb, joined by a hyphen: *Levanto-me às sete.* After *não, nunca, já, também, que* and question words it comes before the verb: *Não me levanto cedo. Acho que me levanto às sete.*
With *ir* and most verbs the pronoun joins the infinitive: *Vou levantar-me às sete.* After *de, para, sem* it often goes before it: *Tenho de me levantar. Para me levantar cedo, deito-me cedo.*
With the body and clothes, use the article, not a possessive: *Lavo as mãos.* (not *as minhas mãos*)

sections.name: With a fixed preposition
sections.what: The preposition belongs to the verb. Learn the two together.
regel: The preposition is part of the verb: *lembrar-se de, atrever-se a, queixar-se de, encontrar-se com.*
After it comes a noun, a pronoun or an infinitive: *Lembro-me da Ana. Lembro-me de ti. Esqueci-me de ligar.*
The preposition stays before a *que* clause: *Apercebi-me de que era tarde.* (not *apercebi-me que*)
In questions the preposition goes first and the pronoun before the verb: *De que te queixas? Com quem te encontras?*
items: Candidatei-me a uma vaga na câmara.
Encontrei-me com o Luís no metro.
Pareço-me muito com a minha mãe.
Já me habituei a jantar tarde.
Apercebi-me de que não tinha as chaves.

sections.name: The pronoun changes the meaning
sections.what: With or without the pronoun, these are almost two different verbs. The English in brackets shows the difference.
regel: *ir* says where you go, *ir-se embora* that you leave: *Vou a casa. / Vou-me embora.*
Some verbs mean something else with the pronoun: *perder o comboio* (miss the train) / *perder-se* (get lost); *lembrar* (remind) / *lembrar-se de* (remember).
*sentir-se* + adjective or adverb says how you feel: *Sinto-me cansado. Sinto-me mal.*
Check the pronoun in the dictionary: *despedir* (sack) / *despedir-se de* (say goodbye, quit).
items: Vou-me embora. (I'm leaving.) Vou a casa. (I'm going home.)
Sinto-me mal. (I feel ill.) Sinto muito. (I'm sorry.)
Perdi-me no metro. (I got lost.) Perdi o comboio. (I missed the train.)
Mudo-me para o Porto. (I'm moving house.) Mudo de emprego. (I'm changing jobs.)
Lembro-me de ti. (I remember you.) Lembro-lhe a data. (I remind him of the date.)
Despediu-se de todos. (He said goodbye.) Despediram-no. (They sacked him.)
Dou-me bem com os vizinhos. (I get on well with them.) Dou um passeio. (I take a walk.)

sections.name: Feelings and change
sections.what: These say that a person's state changes: they get angry, get bored, fall in love. English often uses “get” or “become”.
regel: Feelings often use a pronominal verb: *Zango-me. Aborreço-me. Alegro-me.* The easy alternative is *ficar* + adjective: *Fiquei zangado.*
A preposition often follows: *alegrar-se com, apaixonar-se por, preocupar-se com, zangar-se com.*
*pôr-se* + adjective is a change for a while: *Ponho-me nervoso.* *tornar-se* is a lasting change: *Tornou-se médica.*
